{{Short description|Russian mathematician (1932–2021)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2021}}
[[File:KonstantinovNN.jpg|thumb|Nikolay Konstantinov]]
'''Nikolay Nikolayevich Konstantinov'''  ({{langx|ru|Николай Николаевич Константинов}}; 2 January 1932 – 3 July 2021) was a leading [[USSR|Soviet]] and Russian [[mathematical education|mathematical educator]] and organizer of numerous [[mathematics competitions]] for [[high school student]]s.  He is best known as the creator of the system of math schools and math classes and as the creator and chief organizer of the [[Tournament of the Towns]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.amt.edu.au/imtot.html |title=International Mathematics Tournament of Towns |access-date=18 May 2009 |archive-date=13 September 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090913042234/http://www.amt.edu.au/imtot.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> For his work he was awarded the [[Paul Erdős]] award in 1992.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.amt.edu.au/wfnmcaw.html |title=David Hilbert and Paul Erdös Awards |access-date=18 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231160201/http://www.amt.edu.au/wfnmcaw.html |archive-date=31 December 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Konstantinov was born and grew up in [[Moscow]], [[Soviet Union]].  He graduated from the [[MSU Faculty of Physics|Physics Department]] of the [[Lomonosov Moscow State University|Moscow State University]] in 1954, and later received a [[Ph.D.]] in [[physics]].

In the 1950s, he started  a [[math circle]] in Moscow University and since the 1960s in a number of Moscow high schools.  He continued working with schools developing special classes with mathematics concentration and individual approach to learning.  His students went on to win mathematics competitions on all levels and dozens of them became well-known mathematicians.

In 1978, Konstantinov started the [[Mikhail Lomonosov|Lomonosov]] tournament, a multi-subject science competition.  This tournament is continued every year since then.  In 1980, he started the international [[Tournament of the Towns]] which is now organized in over 150 towns in 25 countries.<ref>"[http://www.amt.canberra.edu.au/mc19912.html Birth of the Tournament of the Towns] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090119102058/http://www.amt.canberra.edu.au/mc19912.html |date=19 January 2009 }}", an article by N.N. Konstantinov, J.B. Tabov and P.J. Taylor in ''Mathematics Competitions'', Vol. 4, No. 2, 1991, pp. 28-41.</ref><ref>[http://www.svoboda.org/programs/edu/2004/edu.060204.asp Mathematics competitions] (in [[Russian language|Russian]]), a [[Radio Liberty]] interview with Nikolay Konstantinov.</ref>

Until his late 80s, Konstantinov continued working in Moscow High School 179 and was an editor of [[Kvant magazine]], a popular Russian science publication.

In 1990, Konstantinov was one of the founders of [[Independent University of Moscow]], one of the leading institutions of higher learning in mathematics in Russia.<ref>"[http://shkolazhizni.ru/archive/0/n-15786/ Why Konstantinov is a legend]" (in [[Russian language|Russian]]), an article in ''Shkola Zhizni'' magazine, 25 May 2008.</ref>

Konstantinov died from the effects of [[COVID-19]] on 3 July 2021, during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]. He was 89 years old.<ref>[https://www.facebook.com/groups/127139657927261/user/100013319475262/ In memoriam of N.N.Konstantinov]</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Arlazarov |first1=V.
